body:
## Problem

The iOS multi-host board currently spends the first board area on two separate horizontal filter rows: one for hosts and one for repositories. On a phone this creates three problems:

1. There are two visually identical **`All`** chips with the same total count, so the scope of each `All` is easy to miss.
2. Long host/repository labels and status text clip at the right edge instead of remaining fully reachable and legible.
3. The top-left navigation/header area is empty after the `Fleet` title was removed, while Settings occupies only the top-right.

This is a UX redesign follow-up to #387, #401, and #423—not a request to restore the old `Fleet` title.

## Physical evidence

Screenshot from the physical iPhone:

- top-left app header area is blank;
- Settings gear is isolated at the top-right;
- host filters: **`All 17`**, **`macbook-air 15 connecting`**, **`Bazzite 2`**; the Bazzite chip is partially clipped;
- repository filters: a second **`All 17`**, **`corral 1`**, **`morsel 3`**, and a clipped **`plush-mead…`** chip;
- the board advertises **`pull to refresh · updates stream in automatically`** below the header.

## Code anchors

- `ios/FleetNotifier/UI/FleetViews.swift:739-788` — multi-host mode inserts the host row, outage summary, then repository row.
- `ios/FleetNotifier/UI/FleetViews.swift:846-879` — the navigation title is intentionally empty and the Settings gear is the remaining top-bar control.
- `ios/FleetNotifier/UI/FleetViews.swift:950-983` — repository filter row, horizontal scrolling, repository-scoped `All` chip.
- `ios/FleetNotifier/UI/FleetViews.swift:1037-1064` — host filter row, horizontal scrolling, host-scoped `All` chip.
- `ios/FleetNotifier/UI/FleetViews.swift:989-1035` — shared capsule treatment and minimum hit target for repository chips.
- `ios/FleetNotifier/UI/FleetViews.swift:1066-1113` — host chip label, count, and connecting/offline status treatment.
- `ios/FleetNotifier/UI/BoardModel.swift:42-80` — host/repository filter state remains two independent selections and must not be silently collapsed by visual redesign.

## Proposed direction to validate

Use the currently empty top-left header space for a compact, product-specific filter affordance and selected-filter summary, while keeping Settings on the right. The design round should compare this with a compact inline rail and choose the smallest interaction that keeps every host and repository reachable on a phone.

Do not restore a generic `Fleet` title. Do not hide host health or connecting/offline state behind color alone.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No phone-width state shows two unexplained duplicate `All` labels; the scope of any remaining All control is explicit in visible text and VoiceOver.
- [ ] Every configured host and repository remains reachable without clipped labels or counts at the reference phone width; no option depends on color alone.
- [ ] The top-left header space is used for a clear Corral-specific filter affordance or selected-filter summary and does not compete with Settings.
- [ ] Selected host and selected repository state remain visible, reversible, and understandable when both are active.
- [ ] Connecting, offline, and stale host status remains textually available without forcing oversized chips.
- [ ] All controls retain at least 44 pt hit targets and distinct VoiceOver labels (for example, `All hosts` versus `All repositories`).
- [ ] Dynamic Type/accessibility sizes do not produce clipped or unreachable filter choices.
- [ ] The existing independent host/repository filter semantics and composite host-scoped rows remain unchanged unless a locked design decision explicitly says otherwise.
- [ ] Produce a short design comparison with at least: (A) compact header Filters affordance + filter sheet, and (B) redesigned inline filter rail; include phone-sized evidence and the selected direction.
- [ ] Keep this issue design-only until the design direction is explicitly locked; implementation should be a later bounded issue/route.

## Open design decisions

1. Inline compact rail or top-left Filters affordance that opens a sheet?
2. One global All action or clearly grouped `All hosts` / `All repositories` actions?
3. Should the selected host/repository summary sit in the top-left header, inside the filter surface, or both?

## Scope fence

Do not change host/repository data, composite identity, stream lifecycle, grants, stale/offline semantics, or Settings destructive controls. Do not restore the removed `Fleet` title as a generic label. Do not route implementation while Corral is paused; this issue is filed for design clarification and later bounded routing only.

Refs #364, #387, #401, #423.
title: iOS board: redesign host/repository filters and reclaim the empty header space
